strengths: assertive live region on #scene means card prose is announced immediately when a moment appears — the fundamental reading loop works for screen-reader users
first choice receives programmatic focus on card presentation, so keyboard users land on an actionable control without hunting
srTag() injects sr-only emotion prefixes ('Joyful:', 'A loss:', 'An echo:') before log entries, giving non-visual users the same emotional register that colour carries for sighted players
dedicated #stageA11y polite live region announces stage transitions independently of the opacity-animated #stageTitle — a screen reader is not dependent on the visual fade
aria-describedby correctly wires choice hints (the .h span) into the accessibility tree even while visually collapsed, so VoiceOver/NVDA announces the hint alongside the choice label

robust modal focus management: MutationObserver traps focus inside open veils, Escape closes dismissable dialogs (Chronicle, Load, Stock), focus returns to the trigger on close, nested veil stack is handled
roving tabindex on the Chronicle tablist with arrow-key navigation matches the ARIA tabs pattern correctly

prefers-reduced-motion is honoured at three layers: CSS kills all animation/transition durations, scene.js freezes the animation clock entirely (no continuous RAF), constellation.js freezes the twinkle clock, and ui.js suppresses the being-line fade
role=list / role=listitem applied to both the save-slot list (#slotList) and the lineage list (#lineage), with readable button labels on each row
skip link present and functional (#app target), using the standard sr-only-until-focused pattern with correct CSS
inline two-step delete confirm replaces native confirm() — keyboard focus goes to 'delete' button on open, Escape disarms, focus returns to the ✕ button on cancel — accessible and focused throughout
constellation tab panel is keyboard navigable: arrow keys traverse chosen decisions, Home/End jump to endpoints, each decision announces to a polite live region with age, choice, and alt
44px minimum touch targets on all footer controls, slot delete, chronicle/constellation links, and eulogy action spans

contrast of meaning-carrying elements has been progressively lifted from ink-faint (~3.8:1) to ink-dim (~5.6:1) through six review passes, covering chronicle ages, log ages, ancestor ordinals and spans, flow text, slot delete, and star tip alt text
aria-pressed on #flow set to 'true' when fast-forward is active, 'false' otherwise — state change is programmatically exposed in setPP()
setPP() updates both #pp aria-label (pause/play) and #flow aria-label with a full description of current state and next action, covering all three states
blockers: aria-pressed on #flow is semantically incorrect: the element is role='button' and aria-pressed converts it to a toggle button (2-state: on/off). But the control has three states — paused, normal, fast — so aria-pressed='false' during normal play is actively misleading (screen readers announce 'not pressed' while the game is actively running). aria-label already describes state and action perfectly; aria-pressed should be removed from #flow, or the element should become a proper <button> with an explicit state label

The .reflect button (#stockBtn) uses color:var(--ink-faint) at opacity:.82 — effectively ~3.1:1 contrast ratio on the dark background, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 requirement for interactive text. This is a visible, interactive, labelled button and fails minimum contrast

First stage (childhood at life start) is never announced by #stageA11y: scene.js only fires the announcement when lastStage !== null (line 232), but lastStage initialises to null and is set to 'childhood' on the first frame without announcing. Only transitions from childhood onward are announced — a screen reader user begins each new life in silence about what stage they are in

No initial orientation text in the Stars tabpanel before keyboard navigation begins — the canvas is aria-hidden, the legend reads 'drag or arrow keys to roam' but never says how many decisions are traversable. A user with no vision cannot know there are any stars to navigate until they discover that arrow keys do something

improvements.what: Remove aria-pressed from #flow in setPP(); rely on the aria-label alone to communicate state
improvements.why: aria-pressed on a role='button' creates a false toggle-button semantic. The aria-label ('the years are racing by — tap to return to the usual pace') already communicates state and action unambiguously across all three states. Removing aria-pressed eliminates the spurious 'not pressed' announcement during normal play

improvements.what: Lift .reflect / #stockBtn text color from ink-faint (opacity:.82) to ink-dim or ink, and add a visible focus-visible ring that is already used on .btn — currently only .reflect:focus-visible is styled
improvements.why: A labelled interactive button failing AA contrast is a hard accessibility failure. ink-dim (#a99c87) on the dark background clears 5.6:1. The opacity cascade makes ink-faint worse than its raw value

improvements.what: In scene.js, initialise lastStage to a sentinel value (e.g. '') rather than null, and remove the null-guard so the first stage (childhood) is announced to #stageA11y on the very first frame
improvements.why: Screen reader users get no stage context at the start of each life — the first announcement is 'A new season of life: youth' when the character hits 13, with no prior indication they were in 'childhood'. The fix is one-line: set lastStage='' instead of null and drop the !== null condition

improvements.what: When the Stars tab is activated (switchTab('stars')), write an initial count message to #starA11y: 'Constellation: N decisions. Use arrow keys to navigate.'
improvements.why: Without it, a non-visual user has no idea whether there is anything to navigate or how many decisions exist. The count is available as chosenStars.length immediately after build()

improvements.what: Convert the #flow div (role='button', tabindex='0') to a native <button> element
improvements.why: Native <button> gets keyboard activation, correct ARIA role, and disabled-state support for free. Custom role='button' divs require explicit keydown handlers (present but fragile). The flow control is central to the game loop — it deserves a native element

improvements.what: Audit and suppress .entry.whisper from the #log aria-live='polite' region, or accept that it fires and ensure the whisper text is meaningful enough to not annoy screen-reader users who hear every ephemeral line
improvements.why: Ambient whispers ('A long afternoon goes by with nothing in it but light') are added to the polite live region and will be announced. They are intentionally non-informational. Many AT users turn off noisy live regions; if whispers are too frequent, players may disable it and miss actual game events

verdict: A thoughtful, multi-pass accessibility implementation that nails the hard parts — the reading loop, focus management, reduced-motion, and emotion semantics — but is held below 8 by a semantically incorrect aria-pressed that makes the pace control actively misleading to screen readers, a contrast failure on the 'how things stand' button, and a blind spot where the first life stage is never announced.
